description:
LunaPath is a small autonomous rover that scans terrain, builds a hazard map and plans the safest route to a target, even when commands arrive with a 3-second delay, like real Earth-Moon communication. The team is building it for the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge and plans to connect it to NASA lunar terrain data.
A working hardware prototype and phone app already exist. Built on Arduino, it uses an ultrasonic sensor on a servo, Bluetooth control and A* path planning.
summary:
LunaPath is an autonomous lunar landing rocket prototype designed for safe touchdown on the Moon. In real space missions, NASA orbital satellites identify general safe landing zones, but rockets still face local hazards during final descent. Our project solves this critical «last-mile» landing challenge.
Instead of using live NASA datasets directly in this prototype, we built a manual mode where the user selects the target landing zone in our mobile app. Once the target is set, the rocket flies along an arc trajectory, avoids obstacles, and lands safely on its own.
